source_text.body_text:
His success didn't come from wanting it more; it came from accepting who he was and writing from that honest baseline without trying to prove anything.

Manson saw the same law in his own life. The boldest moves he ever made (quitting a corporate job and moving overseas) only happened when he stopped obsessing over the outcome.
other_story_text: Lifting the concept from philosopher Alan Watts, Manson calls this the Backwards Law.

source_text.body_text:
Lifting the concept from philosopher Alan Watts, Manson calls this the Backwards Law.

The harder you chase a good feeling, the more you remind yourself you don't have it. Straining for success makes you feel like a failure.

The moment you stop fighting the burn and accept the discomfort, it loses its power over you.

source_text.heading: The Backwards Law
source_text.body_text:
You burn so much energy trying to feel good that the effort itself becomes the problem.

What would change if you stopped trying to fix your discomfort today and just let yourself feel it?
source_text.prominent_quote: Chase good feelings and they run from you; accept the bad, and it loosens its grip.
